# Lab 28.1: Retail Lakehouse End-to-End

## What We Are Going to Do
Build a complete retail analytics flow: land files in Cloud Storage, model them with Dataform, forecast sales with BigQuery ML, and publish a Data Studio dashboard.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Land raw files.**

bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:cap1
export BUCKET=$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs
for T in orders order_items products users; do
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "EXPORT DATA OPTIONS (uri='gs://$BUCKET/capstone1/$T/part-*.parquet', format='PARQUET', overwrite=TRUE) AS SELECT * FROM \`bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.$T\`"
done</span>
</code></pre>

2. **[SQL] Expose the files as Lakehouse tables (Lab 10.3).** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT` and `YOUR_BUCKET`, and repeat for each table.

WITH CONNECTION `YOUR_PROJECT.us.lab_conn`
OPTIONS (format = 'PARQUET', uris = ['gs://YOUR_BUCKET/capstone1/orders/*'],
         max_staleness = INTERVAL 1 HOUR, metadata_cache_mode = 'AUTOMATIC');</span>
</code></pre>

3. **[Console] Model with Dataform (Module 8).** In a new Dataform workspace with `defaultDataset: cap1`, declare the four raw tables and build:
   - `stg_orders`, `stg_order_items` (views, cleaned)
   - `fct_daily_sales` (incremental table: day, category, country, revenue, orders)
   - assertions: unique keys, non-null dates, revenue ≥ 0

   Schedule it daily with a workflow configuration.

4. **[SQL] Forecast with BigQuery ML.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL cap1.sales_forecast
OPTIONS (model_type = 'ARIMA_PLUS', time_series_timestamp_col = 'day', time_series_data_col = 'revenue',
         time_series_id_col = 'category', holiday_region = 'US', horizon = 30) AS
SELECT day, category, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM cap1.fct_daily_sales GROUP BY 1, 2;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cap1.sales_with_forecast AS
SELECT day, category, revenue, 'actual' AS kind FROM (SELECT day, category, SUM(revenue) AS revenue FROM cap1.fct_daily_sales GROUP BY 1, 2)
UNION ALL
SELECT DATE(forecast_timestamp), category, forecast_value, 'forecast'
FROM ML.FORECAST(MODEL cap1.sales_forecast, STRUCT(30 AS horizon));</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Dashboard.** In Data Studio, connect `cap1.sales_with_forecast`. Add a time series (actual vs forecast by `kind`), a category filter, and revenue scorecards.

6. **Review.** Draw the architecture: Cloud Storage → Lakehouse tables → Dataform → BigQuery ML → Data Studio. Note where you would add data quality scans (Lab 19.7) and lineage (Lab 19.8).

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Ingestion | Parquet in Cloud Storage as Lakehouse tables |
| Modelling | Dataform with tests, scheduled |
| ML | 30-day forecast per category |
| Output | Live Data Studio dashboard |
